paraphrase: With the earth as the lamp's bowl, the surging sea as its ghee and the hot-rayed sun as its flame, I have laid a garland of words at the feet of the one who bears the flaming discus, that the sea of sorrow may pass away.
speaker: Poykai Āḻvār
notes: The opening of the whole Iyaṟpā; with IT 1 and MūT 1 it forms the 'three lamps' of the Tirukkōvalūr story.

paraphrase: Whatever form his devotees delight in, that form is his; whatever name they love, that name is his; in whatever way they contemplate him without blinking, in that way the discus-bearer becomes.
speaker: Poykai Āḻvār
